transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, so... what actually made me call the EAP at work to set this up is that I've just been jumping at everything lately. Every little bang in the office, like a file drawer shutting or someone dropping a coffee mug, it just makes me jump hard. And then my chest keeps racing way, way longer than it should after something like that happens. It's just really starting to bother me.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about a variety of things, like work, health, or everyday responsibilities, even when there isn’t a clear reason to be?

No, not really. I mean, I have normal stress from work—managing my team can get a little busy—but I'm not just sitting around worrying about things for no reason. It's really just... the jumping at loud noises that I mentioned. I don't feel anxious about my health or everyday stuff like that.
Do you find yourself staying really alert or on edge all the time, like you're always waiting for something bad to happen?

Yeah, I definitely do. Especially when I'm in the office now. I just... I find myself constantly keeping track of where my boss is, or looking at where the exits are. I'm always checking to see if anyone is coming up behind me, too. It's pretty distracting, honestly. Even when I'm supposed to just be focused on my team and getting our work done, I'm still doing it.
Have you ever experienced or witnessed something that was really frightening or traumatic, like an accident, assault, or something else that felt life-threatening?
No, nothing like that. I haven't been in any bad accidents or witnessed anything awful like an assault. I mean, I've had normal stuff happen, but nothing I'd call life-threatening or super traumatic.
Have you ever had memories, thoughts, or images related to a stressful or upsetting experience that keep coming back, even if it wasn’t life-threatening?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't have any specific memories or pictures popping into my head that keep bothering me. It's really just that feeling of being on edge and checking my surroundings when I'm at the office, like I mentioned. But no, no upsetting memories keeping me up or anything like that.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places, people, or situations because they remind you of something stressful or make you feel unsafe?

No, not really. I mean, I still go into the office every day. I don't stay home or avoid going to work, even though I feel tense when I'm there. I'm not avoiding my boss or my team or anything like that. I just go about my normal routine... I just feel a bit more on guard while I'm doing it. But no, I haven't been avoiding any specific places or people.

Have you ever had sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, like a panic attack, where you might feel your heart racing, short of breath, or like you're losing control?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't get sudden panic attacks or feel short of breath or like I'm losing control. Like I said, it's really just that constant feeling of being on guard when I'm at the office. But it never spikes into a sudden episode of intense fear or a racing heart.
Do you find yourself getting easily irritated or angry, especially in response to small things, that feels related to this heightened sense of being on edge?

No, I wouldn't say I'm getting easily irritated or angry. I mean, I can get a little frustrated with things at work sometimes, just normal stuff, but it doesn't feel like it's connected to that on-edge feeling. I'm not snapping at people over small things or losing my temper. I'm just... tense, I guess. But not angry.
Have you ever experienced any physical symptoms like dizziness, trembling, or sweating that come out of the blue and aren’t connected to being startled by a noise?

No, I haven't had any of that. I don't get dizzy, and I haven't noticed any sudden sweating or trembling or anything. It really is just... well, just that tense feeling I mentioned before. But my body isn't doing anything weird out of the blue like that.
Do you ever find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things like work deadlines, finances, or other responsibilities, even when there isn’t an immediate reason to be concerned?

No, not really. I mean, I care about my job and hitting my numbers, but I don't sit around worrying about deadlines or money if there isn't a reason to. I handle my responsibilities fine. The only thing that really bothers me is just... going into the office and feeling so tense, like I said. But I'm not an overly anxious person about everyday stuff.
Do you ever find it hard to focus or concentrate on tasks because your mind feels too busy or distracted by that tense feeling?

Yeah, actually, I have noticed that. At work, I'll... I keep opening Salesforce to check my reps' notes, and then I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same account for ten minutes. I'm just not absorbing anything. And even making simple calls, like, uh, figuring out who should cover a client visit... it just feels a lot harder to decide than it normally should. So yeah, it is definitely messing with my focus.
Do you experience this same sense of being on edge or tense in places other than the office, like at home or in public spaces?
No, not really. It's... it's pretty much just tied to the office. When I'm at home or just out and about, I feel fine. I can relax normally. It really just hits me when I'm at work or heading in.
Is there something specific about the office or your work environment that you think might be contributing to why you feel so tense there?

I... I'm really not sure. I've tried to put my finger on it, but nothing stands out. I mean, my team is good, my manager is fine... it's a normal sales environment. There's no specific person or project that's stressing me out. It's just... the physical space itself, I guess? I walk in, and I just feel my shoulders go up. I don't really know why.
Is there a specific object, situation, or part of the office environment that you feel particularly uneasy or fearful around, even if you can't explain why?

No, honestly, there's nothing like that. It's not a certain room or, you know, a specific desk or anything. It's just the whole place in general. I don't feel scared of anything specific there, just... overall tense when I'm in the building.
Do you ever feel this same level of alertness or watchfulness in other environments, even temporarily, like when you're out in public or in new places?

No, not really. Like I said, it's pretty much just the office. When I'm out at a restaurant, or at the grocery store, or visiting a new place... I feel completely normal. I'm not looking over my shoulder or feeling on edge. It's really just when I'm at work.
